script.analysis: All 18,976 stored characters read in two contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Paired hook: two people with $300K net worth both laid off - one panics, one searches calmly. Composite Daniel (46, $300K, all invested, "every dollar should have a job"): $4,200 car repair goes on a card; 27% market drop then layoff illustrates sequence risk at the household level; $78K offer declined because savings allow waiting, then $88K offer. Reframe: ask what decisions money allows, not just its return; cash costs (inflation, opportunity cost); months-of-runway table ($5K expenses -> $15K/$30K/$45K); liquidity test (months without selling, borrowing or asking); two $300K balance-sheet examples ($10K vs $30K cash -> 2 vs 6 months); too much cash ($100K at 25) is expensive; dry powder/opportunities without market timing; tight-credit environments; psychological effect; earn a competitive rate but don't over-optimize; Daniel's resolution. Calm, balanced, well-structured; no community CTA; few statistics. One narrative inconsistency: Daniel is first described as having moved all savings into the market and charging a $4,200 repair, then has "several months" of savings and later "$30,000". ASR ("ear sum") preserved; not audio-verified.
